findings: The canonical authorization subject independently recomputes to SHA-256 4c80a284ca73889c8896b0be34c4db5a6e45927563b6f8ca6012d27805f7f7e4 and binds the reviewed paid path to repository commit f6e9f8fa29f6b7ef7bc7310f0a3ed673ab2665f4.

All 11 referenced source calibration artifacts independently recompute to their declared SHA-256 hashes. Their immutable results support 12 rps as the sustainable one-GPU guard point, 15 rps as the one-GPU overload point, and 20 rps as the sustainable two-GPU reference point.

The integrated v10 configuration and launcher freeze the deterministic reclamation trigger at queue depth 20 and the fail-closed scientific abort at depth 25. The live trigger additionally requires positive queue slope, and postprocessing recomputes the trigger and maximum backlog from the complete offered/completed request evidence.

The global spike and recovery producer remains fixed at 15 rps after GPU1 becomes eligible; the recovery criterion is measured aggregate completed service rate strictly greater than the measured offered rate, not equality to the historical 20-rps reference capacity.

The queue-drain gate samples the complete five-second trend at exact one-second boundaries and requires a negative least-squares slope, lower final depth than initial depth, lower second-half mean depth than first-half mean depth, and completed rate greater than offered rate. Endpoint decrease alone cannot pass.

Restore eligibility is downstream of the sustained drain gate and requires five complete one-second SLO windows, full TTFT cohorts, p95 TTFT at or below two seconds, queue depth at or below the recovery threshold, and a final low-backlog check.

The focused queue, serving-protocol, scientific-contract, and live-driver suites pass 25 of 25 checks against the frozen commit. No reviewer exchange or asynchronous approval wait exists on the live GPU-measured path.
